_doc: Walks to a goal (generated by tools/trails/goal_walks.py from OpenStreetMap, ODbL, and the Copernicus DEM; never edit by hand).

trails.name: Ojos del Salado summit
trails.why: Nevado Ojos del Salado is a stratovolcano of the Andes on the border between Argentina and Chile.

trails.name: Mercedario summit
trails.why: Cerro Mercedario is the highest peak of the Cordillera de la Ramada range and the eighth-highest mountain of the Andes.

trails.name: Cerro Las Tórtolas
trails.why: Cerro Las Tórtolas is a mountain in the Andes Mountains, on the border between Argentina and Chile.

trails.name: Nevado San Francisco
trails.why: Nevado San Francisco, or Cerro San Francisco, is a stratovolcano on the border between Argentina and Chile, located just southeast of San Francisco Pass.

trails.name: Peinado summit
trails.why: Peinado is a stratovolcano in Argentina, which has likely erupted within the past 12,000 years.

trails.name: Cerro Morado
trails.why: Cerro Morado is a 5,000 m mountain in Argentina's Iruya department, near the village of Colanzulí.

trails.name: Planchón-Peteroa summit
trails.why: Planchón-Peteroa is a complex volcano extending in a north-south direction along the border between Argentina and Chile.

trails.name: Cerro Nuñorco Grande
trails.why: Ñuñorco Grande is a mountain in the Cumbres de Tafí, just south of the Tafí valley in Tucumán province.

trails.name: Cerro Catedral
trails.why: Cerro Catedral is a mountain located 19 kilometres from San Carlos de Bariloche, and inside the Nahuel Huapí National Park, in Patagonia, Argentina.

trails.name: Chapelco summit
trails.why: Chapelco, or Cerro Chapelco, is a mountain and massif in Neuquén Province, south-western Argentina.

trails.name: Cerro Mogote
trails.why: The highest summit of the Los Gigantes massif, sometimes called "Cerro Los Gigantes", though no peak has that name.

trails.name: Cerro de las Ovejas
trails.why: Cerro de las Ovejas is a mountain of central Argentina in the Sierras de Comechingones, part of the Sierras Pampeanas.

trails.name: Cerro Piltriquitrón
trails.why: Cerro Piltriquitrón, "el Piltri" to the locals, is a mountain of the Andes east of El Bolsón, in Río Negro province, Argentina.

trails.name: Cerro Belvedere
trails.why: Cerro Belvedere is a hill east of Lago Correntoso, in the province of Neuquén, Argentina.

trails.name: Uritorco summit
trails.why: Cerro Uritorco is a mountain and highest peak of the Sierras Chicas chain in the northwest of the province of Córdoba, Argentina.

trails.name: Cerro Volcánico
trails.why: Cerro Volcánico is a cinder cone in Argentina, located southeast of the massive stratovolcano of Tronador.

trails.name: Cerro Bayo
trails.why: Cerro Bayo is a mountain of the Andes range located 9 km from the town Villa La Angostura, Neuquén Province, Argentina, within the Valdivian temperate rain forests, in an area with numerous lakes.

trails.name: Cerro Tres Picos
trails.why: Cerro Tres Picos is the highest point of the Sierra de la Ventana mountain range in the province of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

trails.name: Cerro Currumahuida
trails.why: Cerro Currumahuida is a peak of the Andes in the Cushamen department, Chubut province, Argentina.

trails.name: Cerro de la Ventana
trails.why: Cerro Ventana is the hill that gives its name to the Ventania range, in the province of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

trails.name: Pico Salamanca
trails.why: Pico Salamanca is a peak near Comodoro Rivadavia in Patagonia, visible from the seafront and the beaches to the north.

trails.name: Laguna Las Chaquiras
trails.why: Laguna Las Chaquiras is a glacial lake in the Minas department, in the north of Neuquén province, Argentine Patagonia.

trails.name: Cascada Los Hornillos
trails.why: The Cascada de los Hornillos is a waterfall in the La Quebrada nature reserve at Río Ceballos, Córdoba, about 3 km from the La Quebrada dam.
